q: What fish live in the Una river?
a: The Una is home to brown trout, grayling and huchen, and in some stretches also rainbow trout, which is an introduced species. Anglers know the Una for its clear water and salmonid species. Many other fish species also live in the river, especially further downstream.

q: Are there huchen in the Una?
a: Yes, the huchen, also known as the Danube salmon (mladica), lives in the Una and is one of the most prized fish in the river for anglers. It is most often mentioned on the stretches downstream of Bihać towards Bosanska Krupa. Special rules apply to huchen fishing, so check them with the local angling club before you go out.

q: When is the huchen fishing season on the Una?
a: Huchen fishing in Bosnia and Herzegovina is generally tied to the colder part of the year, roughly autumn to winter, when the fish are most active. The exact period depends on regulations and the stretch of river, so check with the local angling club. On many beats huchen are fished catch and release.

q: Do you need a fishing permit for the Una?
a: Yes, you always need a valid permit for the beat you are fishing on the Una. Carry your ID along with the permit. Permits for Una National Park are issued by the park, and for stretches outside the park by local angling clubs. It is best to buy your permit before going to the water, as rangers and fishing wardens check anglers.

q: Where can I buy a fishing permit for Una National Park?
a: Daily and multi-day permits for Una National Park are sold at the Tourist Information Centre in Bihać, at the information point in Kulen Vakuf and at the Milančev buk entrance in Martin Brod. Annual permits are issued only by the park administration. Permit prices are listed in the price list on the park's official website, npuna.com.

q: Where can I buy a fishing permit for the Una outside the national park?
a: For stretches of the Una outside the national park, permits are issued by the local angling clubs that manage those beats, for example in Bihać and Bosanska Krupa. Conditions, prices and points of sale vary from club to club. The best place to ask is the Tourist Information Centre in Bihać.

q: What types of fishing permits are available in Una National Park?
a: For visitors, Una National Park offers daily and three-day permits, and five-day permits for the fly-fishing beats. Members of angling clubs in Bosnia and Herzegovina can buy a daily permit with proof of membership, and there are annual permits for local anglers and residents. Prices are given in the Una National Park price list.

q: What are the fishing beats in Una National Park?
a: Under the 2026 rules, the park's beats are Martin Brod with a special section on the Unac, Gečet, Kulen Vakuf, Klisa – Ćelije, Dvoslap and Očigrije. Martin Brod and Kulen Vakuf are fly-fishing only, while the others also allow spinning and fishing with a bombarda. The rules can change every year.

q: Where can you go fly fishing on the Una?
a: In Una National Park, fly fishing is allowed on the Martin Brod beat, including a special section on the Unac river, and on the Kulen Vakuf beat, and on the Gečet beat from Monday to Thursday. Martin Brod is especially well known among fly anglers for its clear water and long calm runs. On these beats all fish are returned to the water.

q: Is fishing on the Una catch and release?
a: On the fly-fishing beats in Una National Park, Martin Brod, Kulen Vakuf and the Unac, strict catch and release applies to all species. On the spinning and bombarda beats you may keep up to two fish a day, and only trout and grayling between 30 and 40 cm long. Outside the park, the local angling club's rules apply.

q: When is the trout season in Una National Park?
a: On the spinning and bombarda beats in Una National Park, brown trout may be fished from 1 March to 30 September, under the 2026 rules. On the fly-fishing beats the season runs from 1 May to 31 October, and on the Unac from 1 March to 31 October. Check the dates each year on the park's official website, npuna.com.

q: When is the grayling season on the Una?
a: In Una National Park grayling may be fished from 1 May to 31 October, under the 2026 rules. Outside that period grayling are protected. Seasons can change from year to year, so check the current fishing regulations of Una National Park before you travel.

q: On which days can you fish in Una National Park?
a: On the fly-fishing beats Martin Brod, Kulen Vakuf and the Unac, you can fish every day during the season. On the Klisa – Ćelije, Dvoslap and Očigrije beats, fishing is only allowed from Friday to Sunday. On the Gečet beat, fly anglers fish from Monday to Thursday and other anglers from Friday to Sunday.

q: What are the fishing hours in Una National Park?
a: Fishing in Una National Park starts at 7 am and ends depending on the time of year: 6 pm until 1 May, 9 pm from May to the end of August, and 7 pm in September. Night fishing is prohibited. Check the exact hours for your dates in the park's current rules.

q: What is the size limit for trout and grayling on the Una?
a: On the Una National Park beats where you may keep fish, trout and grayling must be between 30 and 40 cm long, and fish outside that range must be released. You may keep no more than two fish a day. Outside the park, size limits are set by the local angling clubs.

q: What is prohibited when fishing in Una National Park?
a: Live bait and bread, fishing from boats and bridges, night fishing, catching fish by hand and fishing in permanent no-fishing zones are all prohibited. On the fly-fishing beats only one rod is allowed, with a barbless hook and no added weight. After fishing you must check out with the ranger service.

q: Where is fishing prohibited in Una National Park?
a: Una National Park has seven permanent no-fishing zones, including areas around Štrbački buk, near Klisa, above Dvoslap, and parts of the Unac, Krka and Ostrovica. All forms of fishing are prohibited in these zones. The exact boundaries are set out in the fishing regulations on the park's official website, npuna.com.

q: Do children need a fishing permit on the Una?
a: In Una National Park, children under 13 do not need a permit if they fish under the supervision of an adult with a valid permit. Their catch counts towards that adult's daily limit. Outside the park, the rules for children are set by the local angling clubs.

q: What is the penalty for fishing without a permit on the Una?
a: In Una National Park, fishing without a permit can lead to a temporary or permanent ban from fishing in the park, and the permit is not refunded. Under the 2026 rules, anyone sanctioned the previous year cannot buy a permit for the current year. Fines under the law are also possible.

q: When is the best time to fish the Una?
a: For trout and grayling, late spring and early autumn are best, when the water is clear and the fish are active. In summer, fish early in the morning and in the evening, when the water is cooler. Huchen are traditionally fished in the colder part of the year, roughly autumn to winter.

q: Where are the best fishing spots on the Una?
a: Among fly anglers the best known are Martin Brod and the Unac river in Una National Park, and the area around Kulen Vakuf. For spinning, the Klisa – Ćelije and Dvoslap beats in the park are popular. Downstream of Bihać towards Bosanska Krupa, anglers mostly target huchen. Whichever beat you choose, check the rules and permitted methods before you go.

q: Can you fish in the town of Bihać itself?
a: The Una flows through central Bihać, but even there you need a permit from the local angling club that manages that stretch. The rules and permitted methods may differ from those in the national park. Ask at the Tourist Information Centre in Bihać about permits.

q: Can you hire a fishing guide on the Una?
a: Yes, local fishing guides work on the Una and know the beats and rules, especially for fly fishing and huchen. A guide is worth it if you are fishing the Una for the first time, as they help with permits, choosing spots and technique. Local angling clubs or the tourist information centre can give you guides' contacts.

q: What flies work on the Una?
a: Both dry flies and nymphs are used on the Una, depending on the season, weather and fish activity, and local fly anglers often recommend smaller patterns because of the clear water. On the Una National Park beats only barbless hooks are allowed. For the right choice of flies, it is best to ask a local guide.

q: Is the Una good for fly fishing?
a: Yes, the Una is internationally known among fly anglers for its very clear water, waterfalls and populations of trout and grayling. The stretch at Martin Brod and the Unac river are particularly prized. Fly fishing in the park is catch and release, which helps protect fish stocks.

q: Can you keep the fish you catch in Una National Park?
a: On the spinning and bombarda beats in Una National Park you may keep up to two fish a day if they are between 30 and 40 cm long. On the fly-fishing beats all fish must be returned to the water. The rules can change, so check them before every trip.

q: Is rainbow trout native to the Una?
a: No, rainbow trout is an introduced species, and the Una National Park rules list it as non-native. On the spinning beats it may be fished from 1 March to 31 October, and on the fly-fishing beats it is also released. The native species are brown trout, grayling and huchen.

q: Do you need to check out after fishing in Una National Park?
a: Yes, under Una National Park rules anglers must check out with the ranger service after fishing. Rangers check permits and compliance with the rules during the day, so always carry your ID with your permit. Failing to check out can be treated as a breach of the rules. You will be told exactly how to check out when you buy your permit.

q: Can you fish the Una in winter?
a: In Una National Park fishing mainly takes place from March to October under the rules, so it is not allowed there in winter. Outside the park, on stretches managed by local clubs, huchen are traditionally fished in winter according to their rules. Check the dates with the club before you travel.

q: Is the Una a clean river for fishing?
a: The Una is known for its very clear water, and official tests in 2025 confirmed that the river is clean in the Bihać area. Clear water means wary fish, so you need finer tippets and a careful approach to the bank. That is exactly why the Una attracts anglers from all over Europe.

q: How far is Martin Brod from Bihać?
a: Martin Brod is about 50 km from Bihać, via Ripač and Kulen Vakuf, and the drive takes about an hour. It lies in the southern part of Una National Park, by the Milančev buk waterfall. You can also buy fishing permits there.

q: Is Bihać a good base for a fishing holiday?
a: Yes, from Bihać you can easily reach the beats in Una National Park and the stretches of the Una downstream towards Bosanska Krupa. Park permits can be bought at the Tourist Information Centre in Bihać. Our houses on the Una are practical for anglers, and you can send an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com.

q: Can I fish in front of my holiday house on the Una?
a: You may only fish with a valid permit for the beat where the house is located, even if the house is right on the bank. The river near Lohovo and Pritoka belongs to different beats, so check which club or the park manages it. When you arrive, we can tell you whom to contact for a permit.

q: Can you fish from the bank or from a boat on the Una?
a: In Una National Park fishing from boats and bridges is prohibited, so you fish from the bank or by wading. Outside the park, the rules are set by local angling clubs. Take care when wading, as the bottom is rocky and the current is strong in places.

q: What fishing gear should I bring to the Una?
a: For fly fishing, bring a fly rod, waders or wading boots with good soles, polarised sunglasses and barbless hooks. For spinning, a light spinning rod is enough, in line with the beat's rules. Always carry your permit and ID along with your gear.

q: Is live bait allowed on the Una?
a: In Una National Park live bait and bread are prohibited, and only artificial lures, the bombarda and flies are allowed, depending on the beat. Using fish as bait is also prohibited. Outside the park, check the rules with the local angling club. On the fly-fishing beats only an artificial fly on a barbless hook is allowed.

q: Is fishing on the Una suitable for beginners?
a: Yes, but because of the clear water and wary fish, fishing the Una can be harder than on other rivers. Beginners are advised to use a local guide or choose a spinning beat, where the rules are simpler. In Una National Park, children under 13 can fish with an adult who holds a permit.

q: Where can I find the current fishing rules for the Una?
a: Current rules for Una National Park, including seasons, beats and prices, are published on the park's official website, npuna.com. For stretches outside the park, the rules come from local angling clubs. Rules can change every year, so check them before you travel. You can also get permit information at the Tourist Information Centre in Bihać.

q: Can you combine fishing with a family holiday in Bihać?
a: Yes, while one family member fishes, the others can go swimming, rafting or visit Štrbački buk. Distances around Bihać are short, so it is easy to plan the day. The houses on the Una in Lohovo, Pritoka and Grmuša are well suited to this kind of holiday, and you book directly with the owner with no booking fee.
